## Summary

The 68080 has 64-bit D0–D7, A0–A7, FP0–FP7, plus new B0–B7 address registers and E0–E23 general purpose registers.

## Details

The original draws the user programming model as register boxes, with the caption "Legacy model in gray." Widths follow the drawing's column labels (64, 32, 16 and 8 bit). This is the drawing in text:

| Registers | Count | Drawn width | Gray (legacy) part in the drawing |
|---|---|---|---|
| D0–D7 data registers | 8 | 64 bits (columns 64, 32, 16, 8 bit) | lower 32 bits |
| A0–A7 address registers (A7 = SP) | 8 | 64 bits (columns 64, 32 bit) | lower 32 bits |
| PC | 1 | 32 bits (drawn as 64) | lower 32 bits |
| CC | 1 | 8 bits (drawn as 64): the condition codes, the low byte of SR | lower 16 bits |
| FP0–FP7 floating point registers | 8 | 64 bits | all |
| B0–B7 address registers | 8 | 64 bits | none (new) |
| E0–E23 general purpose registers for integer and float | 24 | 64 bits (three columns: E0–E7, E8–E15, E16–E23) | none (new) |

The document owner adds (2026-11-03): the PC is 32 bits wide. CC is the 8-bit condition-code part of the 16-bit SR; SR itself is not part of the user programming model.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have only D0–D7, A0–A7 (32 bit) and FP0–FP7. B0–B7 and E0–E23 are new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DO set the Apollo bit (SR bit 11) when your program uses E registers on a ROM-patched AmigaOS, so they survive task switches. ApolloOS always saves them. See [Apollo bit](apollo-bit.md).
